hook.en: Childhood is gone, the poet says, but not entirely lost. You can still see it, if you look in the right place.

narration.en: Childhood is gone, the poet says, but not entirely lost. You can still see it, if you look in the right place.

body.en: The last stanza changes the question from when to where. The speaker answers that his childhood has gone to some forgotten place, and that it is hidden in an infant's face: the innocence he has lost can still be seen in a very young child. That, he says, is all he knows. The ending is wistful: childhood cannot return, but it lives on in the innocence of babies.

say.en: At the centre is childhood; around it, the themes of the poem.
Innocence is lost as we grow.
Reason begins to question simple faith.
Adults are seen to say one thing and do another.
The child discovers his own mind.
The speaker looks back with longing.

body.en: The poem uses rhetorical questions and repetition: the refrain asks a question that has no single answer. It uses rhyme and simple, everyday language. Its themes are the loss of innocence, the growth of reason and individuality, the hypocrisy of adults, and nostalgia for childhood.

problem.en: What does the speaker mean when he says his childhood is hidden in an infant's face?

steps.en: He cannot find his own childhood any more.
An infant has the pure innocence he has lost.
So childhood survives, but only in the very young.

answer.en: The speaker's own innocence has gone to some forgotten place. He can still see it in the innocent face of a baby, which has not yet learnt reason, doubt or hypocrisy. His childhood lives on only there.
